column1: # phase 7 seeds: error-code encyclopedia records (AADSTS / enrollment / NDR families).
# category is per-row here because this file spans subjects.

column9: desc

Sign-in interrupted because multifactor authentication is required and was not completed; expected after MFA or Conditional Access policy changes and from new devices or locations. The user completes MFA or re-registers methods; this code alone is not an outage.

Token issuance was blocked by a Conditional Access policy. Open the sign-in log entry and read its Conditional Access tab to see which policy failed and why; replay the scenario in What If before changing any policy.

Windows MDM enrollment failed because the user has no valid Intune license or falls outside the MDM user scope. Assign the license or fix the automatic-enrollment scope and retry; the error is user-side and not a device defect.

The receiving side refused the message: a restricted recipient or distribution list; an unauthenticated relay attempt; or the sender failing the destination domain's authentication policy. The exact reason is in the full NDR text underneath the code.

The reply URL in the sign-in request does not match any redirect URI registered on the app. An app configuration error and never a user problem: register the exact URI including scheme and trailing slash on the app registration.

column5: AADSTS50020: account exists in a different tenant
column9: A user from another identity provider or tenant tried to sign in to this tenant's endpoint: typically a personal Microsoft account against a work sign-in or a guest using the wrong link. Send the correct tenant-specific link or invite the account as a guest.

The UPN does not exist in the tenant being asked: a typo; the user signing in with the wrong address; or sync not having created the account yet. Confirm the exact UPN and which tenant should authenticate it.
column10: user not found|upn typo|does not exist

column9: Smart lockout engaged after repeated wrong passwords or sign-ins from a flagged address. The lock releases on its own after the lockout window; investigate the source of the bad attempts before simply unlocking hybrid accounts on-premises.
The password has passed its expiry and must be changed. Cloud users change it at sign-in or via SSPR; hybrid users may need the on-premises change to sync before cloud sign-in recovers.
The account is disabled: offboarded; blocked during an incident; or disabled on-premises with the state synced up. Confirm with HR or security before re-enabling anything.
An application asked for a token silently but no signed-in session existed in the browser. Usually informational noise in the logs; the app falls back to an interactive prompt and succeeds.
The resource demands MFA and the current token does not carry it. Appears when a per-resource policy requires MFA mid-session; the user completes the challenge and continues.
The user must register authentication methods before continuing: they are in scope of an MFA requirement but have never enrolled. Point them at the combined security info registration.

The sign-in needs a device identity claim the client could not provide: typically Conditional Access requiring a joined or registered device while the browser session cannot prove one. Check device registration state and use a profile where the work account is present.

column5: AADSTS50105: user not assigned to the application
column9: The app has assignment required enabled and the signed-in user is not on the list. Add the user or their group to the enterprise application; this is the standard error behind every "I cannot open the new app" ticket.
The credentials were wrong. The overwhelmingly common code in sign-in logs; bulk occurrences against many accounts from one address are password spray and belong to security not the desk.

column5: AADSTS50128: tenant not found from domain
column9: The request carried a domain that maps to no tenant: a typo in the sign-in address domain or an app pointed at a wrong tenant hint. Verify the domain actually exists in the target tenant.
A federated or hybrid user's Active Directory password has expired. The change must happen on-premises (or through SSPR with writeback); the cloud error is only the messenger.

column5: AADSTS50158: external security challenge not satisfied
column9: A third-party MFA provider was supposed to complete the challenge and did not. Look at the external provider's health and the user's enrollment there rather than at Entra.

The existing token is no longer acceptable: password changed; sessions revoked; or too much time passed for the requested action. The user signs in again; expected behavior after any containment action.

The MFA request was denied or timed out: the user rejected the push; entered a wrong code; or never saw the prompt. Repeated denied pushes the user did not initiate are MFA fatigue attacks and go to security.

column5: AADSTS51004: account not provisioned in directory
column9: The identity authenticated externally but no matching account exists in the tenant: sync has not created it or the immutable id mapping broke. A hybrid identity plumbing issue rather than a user mistake.
Conditional Access requires a compliant device and this one is not (or its state has not reached Entra yet). Fix compliance in Intune and sync; the compliance chain runbook walks the whole path.
Conditional Access requires a hybrid-joined device. The machine is not hybrid joined or cannot prove it in this session; check the join state with the device diagnostics before touching the policy.
The app has no consent for the permissions it requests: a new app; new scopes; or consent policy requiring an admin. Handle through the admin consent workflow rather than granting reflexively.
The user was shown the consent prompt and said no. Only relevant when it surprises: explain what the app wants or route to the admin consent request flow.

column5: AADSTS700016: application not found in tenant
column9: The client id does not exist in the tenant the request targeted: wrong tenant endpoint; the app was deleted; or a multi-tenant app whose service principal was never provisioned here. Compare the client id and the authority URL first.
column10: application not found|wrong client id|unauthorized client

column9: The refresh token sat unused past its inactivity window and died. Normal for rarely used scripts and kiosk accounts: re-authenticate and consider a managed identity or certificate flow for anything scheduled.

The client secret is wrong or expired. The classic mistake is pasting the secret's ID instead of its value; the second classic is the secret expiring in production. Rotate properly and prefer certificates.

column5: AADSTS7000218: client assertion or secret required
column9: The token request arrived without a client credential because the app is not marked as a public client while using a flow that needs it (device code or ROPC). Flip Allow public client flows on the app registration or send a proper credential.

Joining or registering the device with Entra failed: the user hit their device limit; device registration is restricted; or the user may not join devices per policy. Check the Entra device settings and the user's registered device count then retry.

Intune enrollment restrictions block this device: the platform is disallowed or personally owned devices of this type are blocked. Check the enrollment device platform restrictions and which restriction applies to the user's group.

The recipient address does not exist: a typo; a deleted mailbox; or the sender's Outlook auto-completing a stale entry. Have the sender delete the cached nickname and retype the address before anyone blames mail flow.

Office 365 could not find the recipient object: commonly a hybrid routing gap where the address exists on-premises but has no mail user in Exchange Online or vice versa. Verify the recipient exists in the directory the message is routed through.

Directory-Based Edge Blocking rejected the address at the front door: the recipient is not in the directory. Frequent when MX points at Exchange Online for a domain whose recipients are incomplete or when catch-all behavior is expected but not configured.
The recipient's mailbox is over quota and rejecting mail. The recipient must delete or archive content or their admin raises the quota within plan limits; senders can only wait.

column5: NDR 5.2.3: message too large for recipient
column9: The message exceeds a size limit on the recipient side: recipient-level or transport limit rather than the tenant maximum. Shrink the attachment or share a link; raising limits is an admin decision with real tradeoffs.

column5: NDR 5.7.133: sender not authenticated for group
column9: The distribution list or Microsoft 365 group only accepts mail from authenticated senders and the message came from outside. Either allow external senders on that group or accept that the block is working as designed.

The destination rejected the message because the sending infrastructure is not in the domain's SPF record. Typically a new sending service nobody registered: fix the SPF record rather than asking recipients to allow-list.

The sending domain publishes a DMARC reject policy and the message failed alignment. Same root causes as SPF failures plus DKIM misalignment; fix authentication for the sending service instead of weakening the policy.

Delivery kept failing temporarily until the message aged out: the destination server was unreachable; greylisting never cleared; or forced TLS could not negotiate. Read the last attempt error inside the NDR for the real blocker.
